### poissonNernstPlanck

The Poisson equation (*PE*) for the validation test, which is taken from [@CHAI20082050], is defined as

$$
\Delta \psi = h^2 \psi .
$$

The mathematical and physical description of this application is given in [@bukreev2024electro1].
The app considers three lattices: one for the Poisson equation (*PE*), one for cation *NPE* and one for anion *NPE*, all of them are of `D3Q19`, which is more precise for the calculation of electric potential gradients.
The ideal case for the *PNPE* system is the analytically solvable Poisson--Boltzmann equation, which describes the Gouy--Chapman model for ionic solutions close to a charged surface.
The *PNPE* system can be written for monovalent cations and anions as

$$
\begin{aligned}
   \Delta \psi + \frac{F}{\epsilon} (C_+ - C_-) &= 0, \\
  \partial_t C_+ - \Bigl( \frac{D e}{k_B T} \nabla \psi \Bigr) \nabla C_+ &= D  \Delta C_+, \\
  \partial_t C_- + \Bigl( \frac{D e}{k_B T} \nabla \psi \Bigr) \nabla C_- &= D  \Delta C_-,
\end{aligned}
$$

whereas the boundary conditions are described as

$$
\begin{aligned}
  \psi_{x=0} &= -0.02\,\mathrm{V}, & \psi_{x=L} &= 0\,\mathrm{V},\\
  \nabla C_{\pm,x=0} &= 0\ (\text{bounce-back}), & C_{\pm,x=L}&=0.01\,\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The ion dynamics is represented with `AdvectionDiffusionBGKdynamics`.
In this application, variables change only in the Y direction, which is why X and Z directions are set to periodicity.
In the Y direction, the *PE* lattice gets `AdvectionDiffsionDirichlet` boundary conditions at both edges.
The ion lattices get the same boundary condition at the bulk side and `BounceBack` at the wall side.
The *PE* can be simulated in the form of an internal loop until convergence in each Nernst--Planck time step, or it can do only one collision per global time step due to the steadiness of the given example.
The calculation of potential gradients, ions' velocities, and Poisson equation source term happens in the `PNPCoupling`.

```{.cpp}
// Poisson-Nernst-Planck coupling
template<typename T>
struct PNPCoupling {
  static constexpr OperatorScope scope = OperatorScope::PerCellWithParameters;

  ...

  template <typename CELLS, typename PARAMETERS>
  void apply(CELLS& cells, PARAMETERS& parameters) any_platform
   {
    T dX = parameters.template get<DX>();
    T velCoeff = parameters.template get<NPVELCOEFF>();
    T poissonCoeff = parameters.template get<POISSONCOEFF>();
    T omega = parameters.template get<OMEGA>();
    using DESCRIPTOR = typename CELLS::template value_t<names::Concentration0>::descriptor_t;

    auto& cellNP = cells.template get<names::Concentration0>();
    auto& cellP = cells.template get<names::Concentration1>();
    auto& cellNP2 = cells.template get<names::Concentration2>();

    T dxPsi[3] = {0.};

    for(int iPop = 0; iPop < DESCRIPTOR::q; iPop++){
      dxPsi[0] += descriptors::c<DESCRIPTOR>(iPop, 0) * cellP[iPop];
      dxPsi[1] += descriptors::c<DESCRIPTOR>(iPop, 1) * cellP[iPop];
      dxPsi[2] += descriptors::c<DESCRIPTOR>(iPop, 2) * cellP[iPop];
    }

    dxPsi[0] *= (-1.*omega*descriptors::invCs2<T,DESCRIPTOR>()/dX);
    ...

    T vel[3] ={0.};
    vel[0] -= velCoeff * dxPsi[0];
    ...
    cellNP.template setField<descriptors::VELOCITY>(vel);

    T vel2[3] ={0.};
    vel2[0] += velCoeff * dxPsi[0];
    ...
    cellNP2.template setField<descriptors::VELOCITY>(vel2);

    T concentration = cellNP.computeRho();
    if(util::abs(concentration) > 1.){ concentration = 0.; }
    T concentration2 = cellNP2.computeRho();
    if(util::abs(concentration2) > 1.){ concentration2 = 0.; }
    T poissonSource = poissonCoeff * (concentration - concentration2);
    cellP.template setField<descriptors::SOURCE>(poissonSource);
  }
};
```

The convergence order of the system is displayed in @fig-poissonnernstplanck-convergence.

![EOC study for PNPE simulations (`poissonNernstPlanck`).](/examples/electroChemistry/poissonNernstPlanck/doc/fig/poissonnernstplanck_convergence.png){#fig-poissonnernstplanck-convergence width="60%"}
